correctness.rationale: The regular body is exactly the intersection of six cube and eight octahedral halfspaces; its 24 vertices are signed permutations of (0,1,2). For every generic central plane, the number of section sides equals crossed facets. Six square facets contribute 2[largest normal coordinate > 2 middle]+2[largest > 2 smallest], and eight hexagons contribute 4+2[middle < 2 smallest]. The resulting indicator formula partitions the ordered-normal chamber into 6-, 8-, and 10-sided regions. Cone generators (2,2,1),(2,1,1),(4,2,1),(2,1,0),(1,0,0) and the standard trihedral solid-angle formula yield the exact arctangents with denominators explicitly verified. The 48 chambers cover sphere measure almost surely. Independently generated facets and edges agree with the analytic count for 10,690 generic integer normals; 80,000 Gaussian directions corroborate the probabilities. These finite checks do not replace the global analytic proof. Excluded vertex-incidence directions are a measure-zero union of great circles.

evidence: The 2024 abstract announces an algorithm to enumerate allowable hyperplane-section counts for arbitrary polytopes, a broader qualitative problem but no Haar angular masses.
The 2016 article restricts sections to symmetry-adapted scans and provides no angular distribution.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general section-enumeration algorithm can in principle be adapted to calculate chambers, but neither the abstract nor the inspected articles supplies this object-specific probability vector. Enumerating admissible side numbers does not logically imply their normalized spherical-cone measures without additional geometry. The uninspected full 2024 article leaves a residual coverage risk.

originality.rationale: The candidate concerns the complete, exact Haar measure distribution of the number of sides of the bounded regular truncated-octahedron central section. The closest full primary work on this exact polyhedron (De Leo 2005) concerns foliations of an infinite periodic extension rather than bounded central sections; the full Coxeter-section article (Valiunas et al. 2016) studies symmetry-axis scans. More recent broad enumeration of section vertex counts does not itself establish an orientation measure, and exact Haar laws for the icosahedron/four-cube concern other bodies. General angle-integration machinery is acknowledged. A mathematically equivalent older formula remains possible and is not ruled out by absence in searches.
residual_risks: The complete 2024 general hyperplane-section paper was not inspected and may contain relevant specific numerical classifications, although its accessible abstract makes no Haar-measure assertion.
An equivalent polygon-type distribution could occur in older crystallographic stereology tables or under an unsearched synonym; absence from searches is not a proof of historical originality.
The two related published exact Haar section records for different polyhedra were available through searchable summaries, not full repository documents.

value.rationale: The regular truncated octahedron is the natural Archimedean space-filler and BCC lattice Voronoi cell. A uniform orientation through its center defines a canonical stereological statistic, rather than an arbitrarily selected slice. The finding determines the entire probability law, including sharp exclusion of plausible 4- and 12-gon section types and exact positive measures of the three realized types. Deriving the exact spherical-angle partition is necessary beyond knowing the polytope face list. The claim does not need a broader downstream theorem to be a mathematically meaningful complete classification.
